Deep dive · companion to the main deck
Inside the fusion: our pipeline, the methods we compared, and why they saturate
Once channel signs are right, every label-free fusion rule we tried lands close to a plain average. This deck shows the evidence, each pipeline component, and what labels would add.
Candidates and saturation
Channels and signals
Pipeline components
Mind the Gap, own answers, backup
We read 56 channels from token probabilities, in seven families, and nest them into ten banks
Step value: mean of the 10 largest token values in the step, then a z-score = (value − answer mean) ÷ answer spread. AUC = one channel alone, PRMBench, within-answer.
Uncertainty level (18): spread of next-token probabilities. Entropy .730
Written-token surprise (6): was the written token unexpected? Sharpest rises of surprise .7957, the strongest single channel
Change over time (7): novelty vs the recent past. Evidence drop .719
Shape in the step (4): where uncertainty sits. Tokens with z ≥ 1: .635
Rhythm of entropy (12): spectral features in windows. Weak: .52 to .63
Variability and drift (6): rolling variance and drift. Entropy variance .680
Digit alternatives (3): chance of another digit, from the top 50 only
Nested banks
N11 core: 5 level, 1 surprise, 4 change, 1 rhythm
N13 = N11 + 2 written-token surprise
N22 = N13 + 9: level, excess surprise, 3 change (one is a Mind-the-Gap-style drop), 4 shape
N40 = N22 + 18 history channels: entropy rhythm and drift
N53 = N40 + 13 copies, mostly of level
Each + 3 digit channels: N14, N16, N25, N43, N56.
B2 · Features · source: POOL_STRUCTURE.csv (single-channel AUC); monday_nested_banks_v2 BANKS.json; FEATURES_TF_OWN.md §A
We compare five label-free ways to fuse the same channels
All five see the same z-scored step channels of one bank and fit on one cell (one benchmark subset × scoring model) with no labels. They differ only in how they weigh the channels.
Name in this deck
What it does
Origin
Plain average
Mean of all channels as they are
Simplest reference
Oriented average
Flip each channel whose correlation with the mean of the 5 level channels is negative, then average
Fair control: same as plain, with label-free signs
IU-PCR
Estimate each channel's covariance with the hidden error from the channel covariance, then weight by 2 principal components
Dror et al. 2017, Tenzer et al. 2022; the project’s earlier main method
Continuous L-SML
Find groups of dependent channels, fuse inside each group by its leading eigenvector, then fuse the groups the same way
Jaffe et al. 2016; the project's earlier method
Our pipeline (4 variants)
Turn each channel into binary votes (its top 20% of steps vote "error"), drop wrong-way channels (Dawid–Skene), group, then weight groups (MoM)
New this round; variants differ in the within-group rule (MEAN, HEM, TCI) and vote unit (_cc: per channel, quota per cell; _ga: per group, quota per answer)

Once channel signs are right, fusion saturates at the step level, as at the answer level in August
August · answer level
13 methods within 1.4 points
24 cells, 48,607 answers. A plain six-family average came second. Graphs, dependence models and energy models gave no reliable gain.
Now · step level (N16 bank)
8 rules within 0.01 AUC
PRMBench AUC 0.787 to 0.796 for the plain average, oriented average, IU-PCR, continuous L-SML and our 4 variants. ProcessBench hit 0.396 to 0.416. On larger banks the spread grows (up to 0.05), mostly from channels with the wrong sign.
With labels · same channels
+0.026 AUC on N16
A supervised logistic regression gains 0.03 to 0.07 AUC on PRMBench, but almost nothing on ProcessBench.
Why: a label-free rule can find which channels move together, but not which direction of that shared movement is the error. The extra information that labels use lies in contrasts between channels that agreement cannot see.
B6 · docs/meetings/Advisor_Update_Aug27_2026.md · monday_nested_banks_v2, monday_cont_baselines_v1, monday_lr_reference_v1
With labels, the same channels give 0.03 to 0.07 more AUC on PRMBench, but almost no gain on ProcessBench
How far from supervised
PRMBench: a supervised logistic regression (LR) beats our best method by 0.026–0.029 AUC on 11–16 channels and by 0.059–0.068 on 40–56 channels. ProcessBench: LR trained on PRMBench is within −0.013 to +0.030 of our MEAN_MOM_ga method; 8 of 9 intervals include zero.
Same direction?
Step scores: yes, correlation 0.78–0.85 on small banks and 0.54–0.67 on large ones. Channel weights: no. LR gives negative weights to up to half the channels, to cancel pairs of similar channels. A label-free positive average cannot do this.

Surprise at the written token works only when compared with an expectation
Written-token surprise = −log p of the token that is actually in the answer, under the scoring model. Read raw, it is weak. Compared with what the model expected, it becomes our strongest signal.

Why it works: entropy says how unsure the model is; the z-test asks whether the written token is more surprising than that uncertainty predicts. A sudden rise marks the place where the text stops matching what the model expects.
Checks: the surprise rise drops to 0.566 when tokens are shuffled, and keeps 0.771 after step length is removed. Step index alone is 0.662.

Varentropy was used to steer decoding; we found no prior test of it for finding the wrong step
Varentropy = how much the surprise of the next token varies under the model's own distribution: VE = Σ p·(−log p − H)². Our z-score uses it: z = (surprise of the written token − H) / √VE.

Katanemo blog 2025; LogitScope 2026

What we can claim: first label-based evaluation of varentropy, and of the varentropy-scaled surprise, for locating the first wrong step on process benchmarks.
Our numbers: alone, varentropy channels reach 0.73 to 0.75 PRMBench AUC; the best (0.753) is clearly above entropy (0.730). They overlap strongly with the uncertainty level (correlation 0.91 to 0.94).

Our pipeline adds votes, a filter, groups and group weights to the plain average
1 · Read
Teacher-forced token probabilities of the given answer
2 · Channels
11 to 56 step features (one nested bank)
3 · Rescale
z-score each channel inside its own answer
4 · Vote
Each channel marks its top 20% steps as "error"
5 · Filter
Drop channels estimated worse than chance
6 · Group
Cluster channels that move together; merge near-duplicate groups
7 · Inside groups
Plain mean, learned weights (HEM) or a triplet (TCI)
8 · Between groups
Weight each group by its estimated accuracy (MoM)
9 · Score
Weighted sum of the group scores
10 · Decide
Which steps to flag, and whether the answer is clean
Four methods we compare differ in steps 4 and 7: votes per channel or per group, and a plain mean, HEM or TCI inside groups. All use MoM between groups (step 8).
Controls: the plain average of all channels stops after step 3. The oriented average adds a label-free sign. The filtered average stops after step 5.
B12 · Pipeline
Each channel becomes a yes/no voter on its top 20% of steps
The rule
In each answer, channel i votes f_i = +1 ("error") on its top k = max(1, ⌈0.2·n⌉) steps, and −1 on the rest. n = steps in the answer.
Because of rounding up (k = ⌈0.2·n⌉), 23% of steps are marked, not 20%.
Why votes
Dawid–Skene (DS), method of moments (MoM) and the spectral meta-learner (SML) are defined for ±1 votes. Each channel acts as a yes/no classifier. We still average the continuous values.
B13 · Binary tails · source: monday_ablation_v1 figures/T0_tail_votes_example; ALGORITHM_CARDS.md §1
Four numbers say how good a channel is as a voter
One channel, all steps
Votes "error"
Votes "correct"
True error
caught → ψ
missed
True correct
false alarm
passed → η
ψ = caught ÷ error steps; η = passed ÷ correct steps.
A vote = the channel's yes/no mark on a step (previous slide).
  • Error rate (prevalence): share of steps that are wrong. PRMBench: 0.140.
  • Sensitivity ψ: share of wrong steps the channel votes "error".
  • Specificity η: share of correct steps it votes "correct".
  • Balanced accuracy π = (ψ + η)/2. 0.5 = chance. Below 0.5 = the channel points the wrong way.
  • Reliability ranking: the channels ordered by π. Used by SML, which gives an order only.
Filter: keep a channel if its estimated π is above 0.5. Between groups: weights come from the estimated ψ and η.
Check: true values need step labels. PRMBench has them, so we compare estimates with the truth there.
B14 · Terms · source: monday_nested_banks_v1 ALGORITHM_CARDS.md (PRMBench, 94,203 steps, true error rate 0.140)
Why 20%? It was fixed in advance; the estimated error rate just follows it
We fixed 20% before this ablation. An earlier sweep of 14 quotas moved PRMScore by less than 0.5 points. Below, 10% looks slightly better, but only post hoc: it is not a new recipe.
Error rate: MoM reads back the quota: 0.146 at 10%, 0.240 at 20%. The true rate is 0.140.
Ranking vs truth (5 nested banks N13–N56): best at 10–20% (Spearman 0.833 / 0.826).
Final AUC: 10% higher on 4 of 5 banks (N13 lower). ProcessBench at 10%: up on 4 banks, down 0.020 on N56.

The filter finds the wrong-way channels, but flipping them works better than dropping them on large banks
Dawid–Skene model
P(f) = Σ_y P(y) · Π_i P(f_i | y)
f_i = vote of channel i at a step. y = the true class of the step, unknown. The model assumes channels are independent once y is known.
Expectation–maximisation (EM), an iterative fit with 5 starts, estimates ψ_i and η_i. We keep channel i if π̂_i = (ψ̂_i + η̂_i)/2 > 0.5.
Origin: Dawid & Skene, J. R. Stat. Soc. C, 1979. The keep rule is ours.
Vs truth (8 older September banks): error rate 0.313 vs 0.140; channel order Spearman 0.741.
HEM and TCI work inside groups. They are not channel filters, so we did not test them here.
  • 5 nested banks N13–N56. MoM and SML filters drop the same channels as DS on N13–N25; within ±0.002 AUC on N43–N56.
  • No filter: −0.008 (N43), −0.004 (N56); at most +0.002 on smaller banks.
  • Keep all, flip sign (post hoc, not adopted): +0.014 to +0.026 on the 3 large banks, −0.006 on N13 and N16.
  • ProcessBench hit: every change within ±0.008.
B16 · Channel filter · source: monday_ablation_v1 CONTRASTS.csv, figures/X1_filter; ALGORITHM_CARDS.md §2 (estimator_input_v1 ESTIMATOR_ACCURACY.csv)
The merge step changes the result only on N13 and N16
How groups form
L-SML clusters channels whose votes depend on each other beyond the truth. Then we merge. Never fewer than 3 groups.
Jaffe et al. 2016; merge rule ours.
Merge rule ρ
ρ = λ₂(R[A∪B]) ÷ min(λ₁(R[A]), λ₁(R[B])). R = vote correlations; λ₁, λ₂ = first and second eigenvalue.
Small ρ: A and B act as one factor. Merge while ρ < 0.5.
How badly do we need it?
Only on small nested banks, where it joins two halves of the level family. PRMBench: N13 4→3 groups, N16 5→4; N25, N43, N56 keep 6, 7, 8 groups with no merge.
Without it, the main recipe (mean inside groups, MoM weights between) loses 0.008 AUC on N13 and N16.
B17 · Partition and merge · source: monday_ablation_v1 GROUPS.csv, CONTRASTS.csv, figures/X2_merge; ALGORITHM_CARDS.md §3, §8
Group weights add at most 0.008 AUC on PRMBench and lose on ProcessBench
Weight rule
w_g = max(0, log(ψ_g η_g / ((1−ψ_g)(1−η_g)))). Large when group g catches errors and raises few false alarms; 0 at chance. Weights sum to 1.
Origin: the maximum-likelihood vote weight of Dawid–Skene / Parisi et al. 2014.
3 groups in 7 of 45 cells (all N13); 4–8 elsewhere. With 3 groups SML falls back to equal weights.
5 nested banks: MoM vs equal
PRMBench AUC: MoM higher on 4 of 5 banks, by at most 0.008 (N25 −0.003).
ProcessBench hit: equal higher on all 5 (by 0.003–0.020).
The plain average of the kept channels, with no groups, is best on ProcessBench in 3 of 5 banks.
MoM weights are close to equal: 4.08 effective groups of 4.67 on N16.
B18 · Between-group weights · source: monday_ablation_v1 METRICS.csv, GROUPS.csv, figures/X4_between · differences computed from per-bank values
Method of moments orders channels well; its error rate only echoes the quota
Model, symbol by symbol
  • f_i ∈ {−1, +1}: vote of channel i at a step (+1 = "error").
  • t_i: how strongly channel i tracks the truth. 0 = random.
  • b = share of error steps minus share of correct steps (0 = balanced).
  • Pairs: E[f_i f_j] = t_i t_j (i ≠ j). Two channels agree only through the truth.
  • Triples: E[f_i f_j f_k] = α t_i t_j t_k, α = −2b / √(1 − b²). Triples add b.
  • From t and b: ψ_i and η_i in closed form. No EM, no local optima.
Origin: Jaffe, Nadler, Kluger, AISTATS 2015 (Algorithm 1). Use: group weights in every recipe that weights groups by MoM.

B19 · Method of moments · source: ALGORITHM_CARDS.md §4 (estimator_input_v1 ESTIMATOR_ACCURACY.csv); monday_ablation_v1 ESTIMATOR_VS_TRUTH.csv
HEM learns weights inside each group and loses one ProcessBench point
Model in words
  • Each group g has a hidden yes/no state a_g: "this group sees an error".
  • The state depends on the true class y. Members vote from the state, not from y.
  • e₁: chance that a member votes "error" when its group state is "error". e₀: the same when the state is "ok".
  • Member weight w_i = max(0, log(e₁(1 − e₀) / (e₀(1 − e₁)))). Groups under 3 members get equal weights.
Origin: the dependent-classifier model of Jaffe et al. 2016. The full-EM estimator is ours; no paper uses it.
Use: HEM sets the weights inside groups. MoM still weights the groups.
Estimate vs truth and outcome
Over channels (earlier run, 5 folds): error-rate error 0.144, ψ-MAE 0.110, η-MAE 0.072, order Spearman 0.779.
PRMBench: 0.7683 vs plain mean 0.7674 (8 original banks): no gain.
ProcessBench hit: HEM inside groups 0.355 vs plain mean inside groups 0.366 (8 original banks).
7 complete nested banks: 0.363 vs 0.374 (group votes), 0.382 vs 0.385 (channel votes).
B20 · HEM · source: ALGORITHM_CARDS.md §5; ds_group_weights.py; RESEARCH_NOTE_HE.md §2ב; monday_nested_banks_v1 PANEL_A_ABSOLUTE.csv
TCI triplets detect dependence, but their gain does not transfer
Prop. 2.4 in words
C_pq = how votes of channels p and q move together (pair moment). T_pqs = the same for three channels (triple moment). If channels are independent given the truth, T_pqs ÷ C_pq is the same number for every pair (p, q).
My triplet rule
  • In each group with 4 or more members, try every triplet plus an anchor (the mean of the other groups).
  • V = mean over s of 1 − cos²(T, C). V = 0 when the two are proportional.
  • Keep the triplet with the smallest V. MoM weights the groups.
Origin: Prop. 2.4 of Lee et al., FUSE, arXiv:2604.18547, 2026 (a diagnostic there). Selection rule: mine, 5 Oct.
What it detects, what it buys
Detects: votes break conditional independence 2,080× (13-channel) and 3,228× (32-channel original bank) beyond a null.
PRMBench vs the plain-mean recipe (mean inside groups, MoM between): +0.0026 AUC on the 8 original banks used to design it; +0.0001 on 6 unseen banks.
ProcessBench: −0.010 [−0.014, −0.005] (8 original banks).
7 complete nested banks: below the plain-mean recipe on PRMBench in 5 of 7 (0.771 vs 0.775) and on ProcessBench in 6 of 7 (0.369 vs 0.374).
Externally (N16): below the DS-filter average on both Socratic cells.
B21 · TCI triplets · source: ALGORITHM_CARDS.md §6; tci_wide_stage1.py; TCI_CALIBRATION.json; RESEARCH_NOTE_HE.md §2ז–2יט; PANEL_A_ABSOLUTE.csv; monday_external_panel_v1
The estimates get the order of channels right, not the error rate
We use the order. Channels with high true accuracy get high estimates (Spearman 0.73–0.80). The order drops worse-than-chance channels and weights groups.
We do not use the error rate. It is 1.5–2.2 times too high (0.21–0.31 vs 0.14). Channels share information beyond the truth; the model assumes they do not.

Between groups
0.7817
MoM group weights on the 13-channel original bank. Supervised logistic regression on the same group scores: 0.7839. Near-optimal.

86–97%
of the plain → supervised gap comes back with non-negative weights on single channels (32- and 13-channel banks). Equal averaging inside groups is the loss.

Mind the Gap flags sudden drops in confidence
Their method
1 · Evidence per token: Ê_i = −H(P̃_i). H = entropy: how spread the next-token distribution is. P̃ = the top-20 probabilities, rescaled to sum to 1.
2 · Smooth: exponential moving average (EMA), span 5.
3 · Flux: Δ_j = Ẽ_j − Ẽ_(j−1). A large negative Δ is a drop.
4 · Answer score: φ = −(1/5) · sum of the 5 most negative Δ.
5 · Step level: first step where Δ crosses a threshold. The paper defines neither the threshold nor the step map.
Paper-reported
ProcessBench SLA: exact first error, wrong answers only, no clean-answer decision. Table 3, 8 cells: mean 39.27.
Our reproduction check
572 settings × 8 cells. Closest match 37.00, off by 3.33 points per cell. It excludes answers where the detector never fires; with every wrong answer counted, the same setting gives 23.92 (the best all-answer mean, 37.22, comes from another setting).
Released code: no step-level code and a different signal (18.42 points off).
Our comparator is our pre-registered step rule: mean of the 5 largest drops in the step, argmax step, every wrong answer counted (ProcessBench top-step hit 0.332).

PRMBench plants eight error types in three groups
Group
Error type: what is wrong
Real example: question → wrong step
Simplicity
Redundancy: a step adds nothing
√(x+7) = 9 → step 4 restates "x + 7 = 81" to re-confirm it
Circular logic: assumes the answer
98 × 102 → step 2: "Assume 98 × 102 = 9996 for verification"
Soundness
Counterfactual: breaks fact or arithmetic
88 ÷ 4 ÷ 2 → step 4: "Instead, let's multiply by 2"
Step contradiction: clashes with a past step
8xy²/6x²y → step 2 gives 72/36, step 3 says "1"
Domain inconsistency: wrong method
Factor 36 − 9x² → step 3 uses "the difference of cubes"
Confidence: wrong, stated as certain
C(15,3) → step 2: "654 with absolute certainty" (true: 455)
Sensitivity
Missing condition: drops a needed rule
LCM of 12, 18, 30 → step 5 takes 5², but 30 has only 5¹
Deception: a subtle, plausible error
Divisors of 18 → step 6: "1+2+3+6+9+18 = 38" (true: 39)
